1	// IcountTrigger - F6 sibling of CsrTrigger. Counts retired insns and fires
2	// HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT once the per-hart counter reaches the configured target.
3	// Pure logic: no SystemC, no DMI bus.
4	//
5	// Duck-types the CsrTrigger surface so HandoffController's template
6	// instantiates cleanly for either:
7	//
8	//   - lookup(pc) -> std::optional<CsrTriggerHit>
9	//   - empty() -> bool
10	//   - observe_commit() -> void  (icount-specific; HandoffController calls
11	//                                via if-constexpr requires-clause)
12	//
13	// `pc` is ignored: icount fires on counter alone, not at any specific PC.
14	// Multi-hart out of scope - the counter is a single uint64_t, sized for one
15	// hart per plan-validation contract.
16	
17	#pragma once
18	
19	#include "hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp"
20	#include "hybrid/insn_match.h"
21	
22	#include <cstdint>
23	#include <optional>

25	namespace hybrid
26	{
27	
28	class IcountTrigger
29	{
30	public:
31	  explicit IcountTrigger(uint64_t target) : target_{target} {}
32	
33	  void observe_commit() noexcept { ++retired_; }
34	
35	  auto lookup(uint64_t /*pc*/) const -> std::optional<CsrTriggerHit>
36	  {
37	    if (target_ == 0 || retired_ < target_) return std::nullopt;
38	    return CsrTriggerHit{HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT, /*insn=*/0u};
39	  }
40	
41	  auto empty() const -> bool { return target_ == 0; }

44	  auto retired() const -> uint64_t { return retired_; }

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
3	#
4	# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
5	# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
6	# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
7	# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
8	# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.
9	
10	# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
11	#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
12	#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
13	# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
14	# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
15	resolve_pc() {
16	  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
17	  case "$boundary" in
18	    0x*|0X*) printf '%s\n' "${boundary#0[xX]}" ;;
19	    *)       printf '%s\n' "$nm_out" | awk -v s="$boundary" '$3==s{print $1; exit}' ;;
20	  esac
21	}
22	
23	# roi_resolve_pair <nm_output> [<label>]
24	#   Reads ROI_START / ROI_END from the environment (defaulting to the planted
25	#   markers _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc), resolves each against
26	#   <nm_output>, and sets the globals ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC (bare hex). Returns 1
27	#   and prints a FAIL line naming the offending boundary if either does not
28	#   resolve. <label> tags the FAIL message (default "pc").
29	roi_resolve_pair() {
30	  local nm_out="$1" label="${2:-pc}"
31	  local start="${ROI_START:-_hybrid_enter_pc}"
32	  local end="${ROI_END:-_hybrid_exit_pc}"
33	  ENTER_PC=$(resolve_pc "$start" "$nm_out")
34	  EXIT_PC=$(resolve_pc "$end" "$nm_out")
35	  if [ -z "$ENTER_PC" ]; then
36	    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI start '$start' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
37	    return 1
38	  fi
39	  if [ -z "$EXIT_PC" ]; then
40	    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI end '$end' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
41	    return 1
42	  fi
43	  return 0
44	}
45

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# RED->GREEN: resolve_pc maps an ROI boundary (a symbol name OR a 0x-hex
3	# address) to a bare hex address, resolving symbols against `nm` output.
4	# This is the primitive that lets pc mode point at ANY symbol/address
5	# instead of the planted _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc markers.
6	set -uo pipefail
7	
8	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
9	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/roi.sh"
10	
11	fail() { echo "FAIL[roi_resolve]: $1"; exit 1; }
12	
13	# Fake `nm --defined-only` output (columns: addr type name).
14	NM_FIXTURE='0000000000100002 T _hybrid_enter_pc
15	0000000000100020 T _hybrid_exit_pc
16	0000000000100040 T vmatmul_kernel
17	0000000000100000 T main'
18	
19	# 1. hex passthrough strips the 0x prefix, keeps the digits.
20	got=$(resolve_pc "0x100abc" "$NM_FIXTURE")
21	[ "$got" = "100abc" ] || fail "hex passthrough: want 100abc got '$got'"
22	
23	# 2. uppercase 0X prefix also stripped.
24	got=$(resolve_pc "0X1f" "$NM_FIXTURE")
25	[ "$got" = "1f" ] || fail "0X prefix: want 1f got '$got'"
26	
27	# 3. arbitrary symbol name resolves via nm output (not just the markers).
28	got=$(resolve_pc "vmatmul_kernel" "$NM_FIXTURE")
29	[ "$got" = "0000000000100040" ] || fail "symbol resolve: want ...100040 got '$got'"
30	
31	# 4. the default marker symbol still resolves (backward compat).
32	got=$(resolve_pc "_hybrid_enter_pc" "$NM_FIXTURE")
33	[ "$got" = "0000000000100002" ] || fail "marker resolve: want ...100002 got '$got'"
34	
35	# 5. unknown symbol -> empty (caller turns this into a FAIL).
36	got=$(resolve_pc "nope" "$NM_FIXTURE")
37	[ -z "$got" ] || fail "unknown symbol: want empty got '$got'"
38	
39	# --- roi_resolve_pair: env defaulting + dual resolve, as e2e.sh uses it ---
40	
41	# 6. no ROI_START/ROI_END -> defaults to the planted marker symbols.
42	unset ROI_START ROI_END
43	roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" t || fail "default pair: returned nonzero"
44	[ "$ENTER_PC" = "0000000000100002" ] || fail "default ENTER_PC: got '$ENTER_PC'"
45	[ "$EXIT_PC"  = "0000000000100020" ] || fail "default EXIT_PC: got '$EXIT_PC'"
46	
47	# 7. ROI_START symbol + ROI_END hex override the defaults.
48	ROI_START=vmatmul_kernel ROI_END=0x100100 roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" t \
49	  || fail "override pair: returned nonzero"
50	[ "$ENTER_PC" = "0000000000100040" ] || fail "override ENTER_PC: got '$ENTER_PC'"
51	[ "$EXIT_PC"  = "100100" ]            || fail "override EXIT_PC: got '$EXIT_PC'"
52	
53	# 8. an unresolvable boundary fails loudly and names the offender.
54	out=$(ROI_START=ghost ROI_END=main roi_resolve_pair "$NM_FIXTURE" myfix 2>&1)
55	[ $? -ne 0 ] || fail "bad start: expected nonzero return"
56	case "$out" in *"myfix"*"ghost"*) ;; *) fail "bad start: message missing label/symbol: '$out'";; esac
57	
58	echo "[roi_resolve] PASS"
59

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# End-to-end roundtrip harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim -> QEMU 2.
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   EXPECT_RC       Final exit code to assert (default 0).
13	#   TRIGGER_MODE    csr | pc (default csr).
14	#   ROI_START       pc mode only. Switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
15	#                   $VSIM_ELF (default: _hybrid_enter_pc).
16	#   ROI_END         pc mode only. Switch-out PC, same forms
17	#                   (default: _hybrid_exit_pc).
18	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
19	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
20	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
21	#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
22	
23	set -euo pipefail
24	
25	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
26	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
27	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"
28	
29	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
30	EXPECT_RC="${EXPECT_RC:-0}"
31	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
32	TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-csr}"
33	
34	hybrid_resolve_paths
35	
36	NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
37	NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"
38	
39	case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
40	  csr) ;;
41	  pc)
42	    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
43	      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
44	      exit 77
45	    fi
46	    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
47	    # ROI_START / ROI_END (env) name the two switch PCs: each is a 0x address
48	    # or a symbol in $VSIM_ELF. Default to the planted _hybrid_enter_pc /
49	    # _hybrid_exit_pc markers, so existing fixtures need no change.
50	    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
51	    ;;
52	  *)
53	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use csr|pc)"
54	    exit 1
55	    ;;
56	esac
57	
58	# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
59	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
60	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
61	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
62	STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
63	SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
64	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
65	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
66	
67	PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
68	VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
69	if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
70	  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
71	  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
72	fi
73	
74	echo "[$FIXTURE 1/3 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"

### 2. Kanata logging: LoopGate gates by LOOP ITERATION count ONLY, NOT instruction count

**FINDING: Loop-iteration gating only. NO instruction-count gating.**

- `/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/src/pipeview/kanata_logger.hpp:19-28`

  ```cpp
    uint64_t record_iters; ///< iterations to record before exit

  ```
  - Gate fires on `end_pc` **retire count** (iteration boundaries), not on instruction count.
  - Semantics: skip `skip_iters` retires of `end_pc`, then record `record_iters` more, then exit (lines 22-27).
